chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', from al-Muthanna, from al-Hasan al-Sayqal, who said:

I said to Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام: A man performed tayammum, then stood to pray, and a river passed by him after he had already prayed one rak'ah. He said: “Then let him perform ghusl and begin the prayer anew.” So I said: He has already completed all of his prayer. He said: “He does not repeat.”

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have already discussed earlier the meaning of this report, and it is possible that the report is to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation and requirement.

key_terms.تَيَمَّمَ: performed tayammum as a substitute purification
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ: he does not repeat the prayer
key_terms.نَهَرٌ: a river, meaning accessible water became available
key_terms.يَسْتَقْبِلِ الصَّلَاةَ: begin the prayer anew from its start

ai.seo_question: If someone performs tayammum and then finds water during salat, must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of one who begins salat with tayammum and then gains access to water during the prayer. The Imam عليه السلام distinguishes between finding water before completing the prayer, in which case he restarts after ghusl, and after completing it, in which case he does not repeat. The closing note states that the instruction to restart may be understood as recommended rather than strictly obligatory.
